image_description: A close-up, eye-level shot of a Nile crocodile resting on a sandy bank. The head and upper torso are visible, with the snout extending towards the right. The skin texture is highly detailed, showing rough, armored scutes on the top of the head and back, transitioning to smaller, yellowish scales on the lower jaw and neck. One eye is clearly visible, golden with a vertical slit pupil. A single tooth from the lower jaw protrudes upwards, fitting into a notch in the upper jaw. The background consists of blurred water.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and triangular with a V-shaped snout (narrower than alligator).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The snout tapers distinctly to a point, consistent with the V-shape of a crocodile rather than the U-shape of an alligator. The head structure appears broad and robust.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The jaws appear thick and powerful. At least one prominent lower tooth is visible piercing the upper jaw line, which is a key diagnostic feature of crocodiles. Other teeth are implied by the jaw line but not all individually distinct due to the angle.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The eye is located on the top surface of the skull. The pupil is clearly a vertical slit. The nictitating membrane is not clearly deployed (eye is open), but the position and pupil shape are correct.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The very tip of the snout is either cut off by the frame or obscured by the angle and sand, making the nostrils impossible to verify definitively.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the body shows heavy armor plating (scutes) and implies an elongated form typical of crocodilians.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal surface displays large, irregular but roughly aligned bony plates with a rough texture, consistent with osteoderms.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The coloration is a mix of dark grey and muddy brown, and the texture is visibly rough and pebbled.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The lower jaw and neck area show significantly smaller, smoother scales that are yellowish/tan in color, contrasting with the dorsal armor.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: No limbs are visible in this close-up crop of the head and shoulders.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is not visible in the frame.

artifact_observations.location: Transition zone between lower jaw and sand
artifact_observations.reasoning: There is a slight softness/blurring where the lower jaw meets the sand, potentially indicating minor edge bleeding or depth-of-field inconsistency, though it could also be natural focus falloff.

artifact_observations.location: Left edge of the image (back of head)
artifact_observations.reasoning: The texture of the scutes becomes slightly less defined and 'mushy' towards the far left edge, losing some of the crisp geometric definition seen in the center.
